## What this is

PR 3 of the diary stack (on top of #4): the auto-diary route no longer stops at opening its PR — it hands off to the orchestrator, which runs the standard chain the framework already ships:

```
compose PR → review → (SHIP + AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVE) → self-approve
          → (approved + AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE) → self-merge → deploy
```

Rework verdicts route into `fix-pr` → re-review per the existing heuristics; `HUMAN_DECISION` with self-approve off stops cleanly.

## Changes

- `agent-auto-diary.yml`: one new `Orchestrate automation handoff` step after PR creation (same `dispatch-agent-orchestrator.js` envelope as `agent-implement.yml`, `SOURCE_ACTION=implement`, heuristics mode, guarded on a PR actually existing).
- README: documents the two opt-in variables and the `AGENT_SCHEDULE_POLICY` kill-switch.

## Safety

Merging this changes nothing by itself: **both `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVE` and `AGENT_ALLOW_SELF_MERGE` default to false**, so the chain stops at the agent review until the variables are set. The content-only guard from #4 runs before the PR ever opens, and self-approval remains provenance-checked (trusted review synthesis + current-head match) inside the framework workflows.

Suggested rollout: merge the stack → manually dispatch `Agent / Auto Diary` → watch the PR stop at review → flip the two vars → dispatch again and watch it land hands-free.

## Validation

Workflow YAML parses (`ruby -ryaml`), `workflow-action-validation` suite passes, README prettier-clean.
